prompt: Write part of a deposition transcript (about 400 words) of a plaintiff in a car accident lawsuit. The defense lawyer asks (lines start with 'Q:') and the plaintiff answers (lines start with 'A:'). Accident: sideswipe while changing lanes in Conroe, Texas. Injury: neck strain. Ask about the accident, treatment and daily life. No names, dates or amounts. (Internal reference C-1113; do not mention it.)
text:
Q: Please state your full name for the record.

A: I'd rather just say I'm the plaintiff in this case. I'd prefer not to put my full name on a transcript that's going to be read by people I don't know.

Q: Understood. Let's proceed with the basics. Where were you on the day of the collision?

A: I was driving on the frontage road near the shopping center in Conroe, Texas. I was headed toward the freeway entrance.

Q: What were you doing right before the impact?

A: I was in the right lane, going about the speed limit. Traffic was moderate. I had my turn signal on because I needed to move left to get over for the exit ramp.

Q: And what happened next?

A: The other driver was in the left lane, and as I started to move over, their car came into my lane. It was a sideswipe. I felt a hard shove on the driver's side and the car pulled toward the curb.

Q: Did the other driver stop?

A: They pulled over a little further up. We exchanged information and a police officer came out to the scene and wrote up a report.

Q: Did you feel any pain at the scene?

A: Not right away. I was shaken up and my adrenaline was going. By that evening my neck was stiff, and by the next morning I could barely turn my head to check my blind spot.

Q: Did you seek medical treatment?

A: Yes. I went to an urgent care clinic the next day, and then my primary care doctor referred me to a physical therapist. I've been going twice a week since then.

Q: Are you still experiencing symptoms?

A: Yes, though it's better than it was. I still get a dull ache at the base of my skull, especially after sitting at my desk for a long stretch. Turning to back up the car is still uncomfortable.

Q: How has this affected your daily routine?

A: I used to go to the gym four or five times a week. I've had to cut back a lot because lifting overhead aggravates it. I also don't sleep as well. I wake up a few times a night because I can't find a comfortable position.

Q: Have you missed any work?

A: I took a few days off in the first week, and I've been leaving early on therapy days. My employer has been understanding, but it's been an inconvenience.

Q: Thank you. We'll take a short break here.
